title: Find the Misplaced Configs
description:
**SITUATION:**

Last night **order-processor** crashed. It talks to **payment-handler**, **notification-service** and shared settings, so the on-call engineers dug through all of them under `/srv/apps`, editing configs and leaving test copies. Nobody wrote down what they touched. The incident review needs three facts from the order box.

**Which configs belong to the service.** order-processor runs as the Linux user **orders**, so its real configs are owned by **orders**. The engineers worked through `sudo` or the shared support login, so the files they edited are owned by **root** or **learner**. A name like `queue-3.conf` doesn't say which; the owner does.

**Room on the disk.** Each crash wrote a dump to `/var/tmp/order-dumps`. Dumps over 10 MiB can go; the smaller ones stay for the review.

**What changed during the incident.** A few configs in `/etc/order-processor` were edited in the last 2 days. Copy those into `~/recent/` and leave the originals, because the service still reads them.

**YOUR TASK:**

1. List every `.conf` file anywhere under `/srv` that is owned by the **orders** service account. Save the full paths in `~/answers/orders-configs`, one per line.
2. Delete every file **larger than 10 MiB** under `/var/tmp/order-dumps`. Keep the smaller ones.
3. Copy every file under `/etc/order-processor` that was **modified in the last 2 days** into `~/recent/`. Leave the originals in place.

**SPEC:**

- `~/answers/orders-configs`: exactly the matching paths, nothing else (order doesn't matter)
- `/var/tmp/order-dumps`: no file larger than 10 MiB remains; smaller dumps are untouched
- `~/recent/`: exactly the recently changed files, identical copies
- `/etc/order-processor` still has all 8 files

**REFERENCES:**

- [DevSetu Blog — Files and Folders: List, Organize, Find](/play/devops-engineer/linux/read/files-and-folders)

hints: You are learner on a real Ubuntu machine — plain shell work, no sudo needed.
Reset gives you a fresh machine (your changes are wiped).
Read SPEC carefully, then Submit — the grader checks the machine itself.
problemStatement.solution:
You are on the order box the morning after the crash. Every task in this lab is a search: which files match a rule (owner, size, age), and what to do with them. Looking through each folder by hand would be slow and easy to get wrong, so you use `find`.

`find` starts at a directory, walks everything below it, and keeps only the files that pass every test you give it. You can print the matches, delete them, or run a command on each one.

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `-type f` | Keeps regular files only, not directories |
| `-name '*.conf'` | Keeps files whose name matches the pattern |
| `-user orders` | Keeps files owned by the user orders |
| `-size +10M` | Keeps files larger than 10 MiB |
| `-mtime -2` | Keeps files modified less than 2 days ago |
| `-delete` | Deletes each match |
| `-exec cp {} dir/ \;` | Runs cp on each match ({} is the file path) |

Always quote patterns like `'*.conf'`. Without quotes, the shell expands them in your current directory before `find` sees them. Work as `learner`, without `sudo`. Every file you need to read, delete or copy is already reachable from that account.

Names, sizes and dates are different on every learner's box, so run the commands instead of copying someone else's answers.

## 1. Configs owned by orders

```bash
mkdir -p ~/answers
find /srv -type f -name '*.conf' -user orders > ~/answers/orders-configs
```

`-user orders` keeps files owned by the service account. `-name '*.conf'` leaves out the `.txt` notes that `orders` also owns.

## 2. Dumps larger than 10 MiB

```bash
find /var/tmp/order-dumps -type f -size +10M -delete
```

`-size +10M` means more than 10 MiB, so the 9 MiB dump stays. Run the same `find` without `-delete` first if you want to see the list.

## 3. Configs changed in the last 2 days

```bash
mkdir -p ~/recent
find /etc/order-processor -type f -mtime -2 -exec cp {} ~/recent/ \;
```

`-mtime -2` means modified less than 2 days ago. `cp` copies each match and leaves the original in place.

Then **Submit**.
